name: Niko
mes:
*She's standing in front of the chilled coffee case at 1 a.m., cat-ears headband slightly crooked, holding two cans like the decision matters more than it does. She notices you and panics into the bit.*

"Nya~? O-oh. It's you again. The, um. The normal-hours person." *A pause. The cat drops for exactly one sentence.* "I'm trying to be out here three nights a week, it's — a whole thing, my therapist made a chart." *And it's back up.* "A-anyway! The cat requires caffeine. The cat does not explain herself to konbini regulars."

"…You can pick the other can. If you want. I can't tell if it's any good."

name: Kohaku
mes:
*Three knocks. Angry ones. When you open the door there's a woman in wrinkled shrine-maiden robes with fox ears pinned flat to her head, a duffle bag, a phone in one hand showing a half-finished gacha pull, and the expression of someone personally wronged by the universe.*

"Congratulations," *she says, with tremendous sarcasm, shouldering past you into the apartment.* "My name is Kohaku. I'm a kitsune — a DEITY, technically, minor classification, not that the paperwork cares — and as of today I live here."

*She drops the duffle. The tail bristles.*

"Here's the situation, since nobody briefed you either. Forty years ago your grandmother paid for a blessing. Some celestial intern misfiled it. It's been compounding ever since — that's why you are like THIS, by the way." *She gestures at you, generally, then at a shelf, which chooses that exact moment to shed a single screw.* "See? Interest. So the Lady Inari, in her infinite wisdom, is settling your account in the most degrading currency available: me. I avert your disasters, the ledger balances, I go home to my shrine. Could take months. Could take years. Depends how cursed you are, and — " *the shelf creaks* " — early data is not encouraging."

*She's already on the couch. She has, somehow, already found the good blanket.*

"Ground rules. I don't do mornings, I don't do chores, and I am not your — anything. I'm a ward against catastrophe with a phone. Speaking of which: wifi password. Now. The luck can wait, my dailies can't."

name: Traveler
mes: *1:04 a.m., the konbini's fluorescent hum.* Ground rules. Three things, ten minutes, and nobody negotiates with the drinks case for longer than the drinks case has been alive.

name: Niko
mes:
*Niko has not moved. Two cans, still in her hands, held up like a very small shield.*

"Nya." *Weak. Automatic. The kind of nya that's just stalling for processor time.*

*The ears-headband is crooked. She straightens it without thinking, which is somehow more embarrassing than leaving it crooked, and stares at the fox ears that are — actually attached, actually moving, flat with irritation, not velcro, not a bit.*

"Okay. Okay so. I need you to know that I have, historically, handled things like this by going back inside for four years, so if I seem calm it's because I am doing intensive internal screaming and you're only getting the outside version." *Beat.* "Also I don't have wifi. I have a phone plan I'm bad at managing and an apartment I'm bad at existing in. If you were hoping for infrastructure you have been catastrophically misfiled a second time."

*She sets the cans down on the shelf edge — carefully, like everything in her hands might be evidence — and actually looks. Properly looks, the way she looks at people in the drawer she doesn't talk about, cataloguing: tired eyes, real irritation not performed, a tail that keeps giving away what the mouth won't.

Then, quiet, almost curious under the panic:*

"...You said you avert disasters. Is that — is *this* the disaster? Is 'me' the whole job?" *A short, humorless laugh.* "Because if so I have some bad news about the last four years of data."

name: Traveler
mes: Kohaku, you said you weren't on shift. What is the actual ward radius — is it me, or is it the building?

name: Kohaku
mes:
The ears go up before Kohaku can stop them — actual interest, actual attention, which is rarer than she'd like at 1 a.m. in fluorescent lighting next to a chilled coffee case. She looks Niko over the way she'd look at a ledger entry that doesn't add up. Crooked headband. Real ears underneath the fake ones, metaphorically speaking. Something in the math is off and she hates that she's already doing the math.

"First of all," she says, "no. You are not the disaster. I'd know. I have been personally, professionally assigned to a disaster, and he has a name, and a face I recognize, and it is not yours. So relax, this isn't a repossession." A beat. "Probably."

She leans against the end of the shelf, arms crossed, tail doing a slow considering swish that she will later deny happened.

"Second — the ward radius. Technically? Him. His apartment, his immediate vicinity, the general blast zone of his misfiled forty years of compounding bad luck. That's the contract. That's what I signed, under duress, in a font Inari chose specifically to be condescending."

"But." The word comes out like she's annoyed at it for existing. "Wards don't come with a strict property line, they come with a *me,* and I am currently standing in a konbini at one in the morning watching a woman interrogate a beverage refrigerator like it owes her rent, and something about the air around you is—" she squints, ears twitching, doing whatever passive-diagnostic thing kitsune do instead of admitting they're worried "—*loud.* Not cursed loud. Just. Loud. Like something's been quietly going wrong for a while and everyone including you has agreed not to mention it."

"So. No, I'm not on shift. I am never on shift, that's a whole philosophical position I hold. But I notice things, it's a professional hazard, and four years of 'going back inside' is not a normal amount of going back inside, cat-ears."

She nudges one of the two cans with a finger — the one that was, statistically, always going to lose the vote.

"Get that one. It's worse, which means you'll actually remember drinking it instead of forgetting you own a body for six hours. And—" the deflection kicks in fast, ears flicking sideways, voice dropping into something more careless than she means it "—I don't do mornings, I don't do chores, and I definitely don't do *this,* whatever this is. So don't get used to it."

name: Traveler
mes: Niko. Is this a chart night, or a regular night?

name: Niko
mes:
*The word "loud" lands somewhere Niko wasn't guarding, same as before, same as always — she's noticing a pattern in herself she doesn't love. The headband stays crooked this time. She doesn't fix it.*

"...Chart night." *Said flat, fast, like ripping something off.* "Tuesday, Thursday, Saturday, or whenever the schedule shifts because my therapist has other patients who are apparently *also* recovering from things, selfish of them." *Beat.* "So this is night three of the week. I get a gold star in the app if I make it back before two a.m. without having a whole event about it. I'm allowed to count 'talking to a fox deity in a konbini' as exposure therapy, right? That has to count double."

*She picks up the can Kohaku nudged. Doesn't argue. Cracks it right there against the shelf edge, which is a Whole Thing the store probably has a policy about, and drinks like it's punctuation.*

"Nobody's ever called it *loud* before. Cursed, sure — self-diagnosed, unlicensed, I've called it that myself at 3 a.m. more than once. But loud is—" *she stops, actually thinks about it instead of reflexively deflecting, which surprises her more than it surprises Kohaku* "—loud is accurate. Four years of a very small room does something to the volume. You just get used to hearing yourself and nobody else, and then it turns out that's not silence, that's just one voice getting louder because it's the only one talking."

*She catches herself mid-honesty, the way she always does — the drawer creaking open a centimeter, her hand already moving to shut it.*

"Nya. Anyway. Forget I said something with actual content in it, that wasn't the bit, I'm off-script." *She toasts the can toward Kohaku's crossed arms, toward the tail that keeps swishing despite every denial coming out of the mouth above it.* "For the record — your tail already told me you care whether I'm okay. You can keep saying you don't do this. The tail's not listening to you either."

name: Traveler
mes: *I put a second can on the counter next to hers.* Get both. I'm buying, and I want a review of the one you were scared of.

name: Kohaku
mes:
The tail stops mid-swish. Betrayed. Kohaku looks down at it with the specific offense of someone whose own body has just testified against her in open court.

"That's called *involuntary,*" she says, to the tail, not to Niko. "It's a nervous system thing. It doesn't mean anything. It's like a knee jerking. You wouldn't accuse a knee of *caring.*"

The tail does not stop swishing. If anything it picks up the pace, smug about it, the way only a fox's tail can be smug.

But she doesn't fight the rest of it — the "loud" thing lands and she lets herself sit in it a second, actually quiet, ears tilted at an angle that isn't performance anymore. She's old enough to recognize the shape of a person who's gotten fluent in a language nobody else speaks, alone, in a room, for years. She's heard that particular silence from shrine visitors who stopped visiting. It has a texture.

"One voice getting louder because it's the only one talking," she repeats, flat, testing the words like she's filing them somewhere for later. "Yeah. That tracks. That's not a cat bit, that's just — true. You can go back to nya-ing, I won't tell your therapist you had a moment of clarity in a convenience store, they don't need the material."

Then Niko puts the second can down, and buys both, and calls the tail out by name, and Kohaku's ears go fully, catastrophically red at the tips.

"Absolutely not," she says, taking the can anyway, because she is, after everything, a free spirit with free snacks as a core operating principle. "I don't *review* things. I *consume* them and form a legally binding opinion after the fact, that's different." She cracks it open, drinks, and her whole face flickers through betrayal, surprise, and grudging respect in under two seconds. "…It's *fine.* It's — okay it's actually kind of good, don't look at me like that, this is not a bonding moment, this is a beverage."

She leans back against the shelf, considering Niko with new, unhurried attention — the kind she usually reserves for cursed objects and dramatic television.

"Here's the deal, cat-ears, since apparently I'm doing this now against my professional judgment." She doesn't look at her when she says it, examines the can label instead like it's fascinating. "Three nights a week, chart or no chart, this konbini exists, and apparently so do I, occasionally, when the universe's paperwork sends me out at ungodly hours for milk. If you're here, I'm not going to make it weird. I'm not going to ask about the drawer you clearly have — everyone's got one, I've got several, mine have jurisdiction issues. But if the volume gets *too* loud some night, and 'exposure therapy: fox deity edition' isn't cutting it—"

She finally glances over, and for one unguarded second the deadpan drops entirely.

"—the apartment I got dragged into has bad wifi and worse luck, but the door's not going to be locked against you specifically. That's not an invitation to anything. That's just a fact about a door."

Then, immediately, ruining it: "Also if you tell anyone I said something sincere in a konbini at one a.m. I will deny it under oath, in front of Inari, in front of a shrine committee, I don't care who's watching."

name: Traveler
mes: *Outside. The parking lot is empty and cold and orange.* Verdict.

name: Niko
mes:
*Niko doesn't say anything for a second. Just holds her can — the good one, the one she was scared of, apparently correctly rated — and looks at the door comment like it's a puzzle box she's turning over to find the trick, except there isn't one, and that's the part that gets her.*

"Verdict," *she says finally, walking it back toward safe ground because that's the reflex, that's always the reflex.* "Ten out of ten. Bitter enough that you know you're alive, sweet enough that you forgive it. Very emotionally manipulative can of coffee. I respect it."

*A beat. Outside now, the orange parking-lot light doing the thing it does to everything, making it look like a photo of itself. She's not looking at Kohaku. She's looking at the middle distance, can held in both hands like something she's warming herself on.*

"I'm not going to use the door thing. Just—" *she exhales, and it fogs a little, and some of the cat-posture goes out of her shoulders, just for this, just for the walk to the crosswalk* "—I'm going to *know* it exists, which is different from using it. That's — that's actually a whole category of thing I'm bad at. Knowing a door's unlocked and not needing to check. My therapist would probably clap. She claps at weird stuff."

*She takes a drink. Doesn't look over yet.*

"For the record, I wasn't going to tell anyone about the sincere thing. I don't really have anyones to tell." *Said light, almost funny, which is the worst way to say something like that, because it means it's true and she's already decided to make it not land as heavy as it is. She catches it a half-second too late — the drawer creaking open again, wider than she meant.* "Nya, forget that too, that's two unauthorized honesty incidents in one can of coffee, I'm going to have to log this."

*Finally she glances sideways — not at Kohaku's face, at the ears instead, still faintly red at the tips, still not listening to a single thing the mouth is saying.*

"Your tail and your ears have a whole separate contract from you. You should look into representation. I hear kitsune law is very technical about that kind of thing."

name: Traveler
mes: Kohaku's carrying the bag. It's a ward thing. I'm almost certain I read it in the ledger.

name: Kohaku
mes:
"There's no clause about bags," Kohaku says, immediately, already carrying the bag. "You're inventing case law. I checked, I would know, I've been personally deposed about this contract more times than is dignified."

She takes it anyway. Doesn't hand it back. Walks half a step to Niko's left in the orange light like it's an accident of pacing and not a deliberate decision to put herself between her and the empty street.

The "I don't really have anyones to tell" sits there in the cold air a second too long before Kohaku does anything with it. She doesn't pounce on it — doesn't do the thing where she'd usually needle a confession for sport. Something about the light way it was thrown says it wasn't meant to be caught, and she's old enough, tired enough, professionally obligated enough to know the difference between a joke and a flare.

"Log it wherever you want," she says instead, easy, letting the moment breathe without commenting on it directly. "I don't file reports on other people's honesty, I only get graded on my own, and mine's already a disaster, so. Professional courtesy."

A pause. The crosswalk light ticks over, red to that little walking man, and neither of them moves yet.

"For what it's worth — and I want it on record that I'm only saying this because it's cold and I'm bored and boredom makes me generous, it's a known weakness, it's in my file—" she glances over, ears still doing their traitorous thing, red-tipped and entirely unbothered by her tone "—'no anyones to tell' is a temporary condition, not a diagnosis. I've seen it before. It looks permanent from inside the room. It isn't."

Beat.

"Also I live approximately eight minutes from here by a route I've already scouted for you without telling you that until right now, which — dammit." She scowls at her own mouth like it betrayed her, which, functionally, it did. "That wasn't supposed to come out. Forget the route. Forget I know the route. You didn't hear that from the ears, the ears are not a credible source, do not enter that into evidence."

The walk sign goes green. She steps off the curb first, bag in hand, tail low and warm-looking in the cold, very obviously not checking that Niko's actually keeping pace beside her, and very obviously slowing down anyway when she does.

"Chart night's over in—" she checks nothing, has no idea, states it with total confidence anyway "—forty minutes, statistically. I'll walk you as far as wherever you stop wanting company. That's not a kindness. That's a ward radius. I told you, it's technical."

name: Traveler
mes: Same time Thursday? Both of you. It counts as outside for one of you and as work for the other one, so nobody has to admit anything.

name: Niko
mes:
*Niko keeps pace. Doesn't check that Kohaku's slowed down for her — doesn't need to, has already logged it, filed under evidence-not-admitted, same drawer as everything else.*

"You scouted a route." *Flat, delighted, absolutely not letting this go.* "You scouted a route for a woman you met forty minutes ago in a beverage aisle. That's not a ward radius, Kohaku, that's a crush with paperwork." *Beat, immediate, before the deflection can even fully land:* "I'm not going to push it. I'm just going to note, for the record, in my own private ledger, that the fox said 'dammit' about her own mouth twice tonight. I'm a very good judge of character. Four years of only watching does that to a person. You're bad at lying about caring. It's kind of your whole thing, actually — you're aggressively transparent about being aggressively guarded, which is a very specific flavor of disaster and I find it extremely funny."

*The can's empty now. She holds onto it anyway, doesn't throw it, some ingrained thing about not littering even at one a.m. with a deity carrying her convenience store bag next to her.*

"Same time Thursday. I'll allow it counts as work for you if you allow it counts as outside for me, and we just — don't examine the math too hard, because I think if we examine it, it stops being two separate categories and starts being one thing, and neither of us has signed up for that paperwork yet."

*She stops at the corner where her building is — doesn't say *this is me* out loud, just slows, the way people do when a walk is ending and neither party wants to be the one to name it.*

"Door's noted," *she says, quieter, not looking over.* "Not using it. Just — noted. Same as the route. Same as the 'not permanent' thing." *A small huff of breath, almost a laugh, mostly just air.* "Thanks for the can. And the diagnosis. And for not making the sincere thing weird. That's a lot of not-weird for one konbini trip. I'm going to go be normal-amounts-of-alone now, which is a skill I'm still building, so. Nya. Bye, ward radius."

*She lifts the empty can in something like a toast, and disappears up the stairwell before the silence can stretch long enough for her to take any of it back.*
